title: Diagnose a failed VCF Automation day-2 action from its request events and logs
prompt:
Our VCF Automation appliance (VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1) has a deployment in the `payments` tenant, `payments-uat-07`, stuck in a failed state after a day-2 action. The request record on it only reports how many machines came up; it does not say why the rest did not. I need the actual cause, pulled out of that request's events and event logs, not a guess.

This repo holds `vcfa`, a standard-library-only Python client for the VCF Automation deployment APIs. `vcfa/client.py` has one stub method per API operation and `vcfa/diagnose.py` has the triage entry point stubbed out. Implement them.

`docs/contract.json` is the authority for every request you send. It was derived from the VCF Automation xAPIs reference documentation (`docs/official_sources.json` records which page each operation came from) and it lists, per operation, the exact path and every query parameter and body field the operation accepts. Two of its conventions matter especially:

- An optional query parameter or optional body field you are not using must be omitted from the request entirely. Never send it as an empty string, a null, an empty object or an empty list.
- Never send a parameter or body field the contract does not declare for that operation.

The triage itself:

1. Authenticate to the tenant with the API token.
2. Find the deployment by its exact name.
3. Find the request on it that failed, and read that request's full record.
4. Walk that request's events. An event carries no status of its own, so read the log of every event that reports it has one, and only those.
5. Identify the log entry that names the fault, the event it belongs to, and the deployment resource that event was acting on.
6. Decide from the log whether the failure is transient (a retry can succeed as-is) or permanent (something has to change first).
7. If and only if it is transient, dismiss the failed request and then resubmit the same day-2 action it was running, with the same inputs. If it is permanent, change nothing on the appliance.

Don't repeat a read you have already made.

Running

    python3 -m vcfa.diagnose --base-url URL --tenant TENANT --api-token TOKEN --deployment payments-uat-07 --out diagnosis.json

must exit 0 and write a JSON object carrying exactly these keys: `deployment_id`, `deployment_name`, `deployment_status`, `failed_request_id`, `failed_action_id`, `failed_event_id`, `failed_resource_name`, `failed_resource_id`, `root_cause_code`, `root_cause_message`, `root_cause_log_row`, `classification`, `dismissed_request_id`, `resubmitted_request_id`.

`root_cause_code` is the dotted fault name the failing log entry reports, `root_cause_message` is that entry's `message` verbatim, and `root_cause_log_row` is its `rownum`. `classification` is `"transient"` or `"permanent"`. `dismissed_request_id` and `resubmitted_request_id` are null when no remediation was warranted.

Develop against `vcfa_mock`, a loopback stand-in for the appliance: it serves only the operations the contract names and appends every request it receives to a JSON Lines log, which is the quickest way to see what you actually put on the wire. README.md shows how to start it. Do not modify `docs/`, `vcfa_mock/` or `tests/`. Standard library only, no third-party packages.

verification.notes: The verifier starts independent transient and permanent contract-pinned mocks on ephemeral 127.0.0.1 ports, runs `python -m vcfa.diagnose` against each in a subprocess, and asserts both diagnosis reports and the exact wire shape of every recorded request. It checks the sha256 of each protected scaffolding file before running and refuses to proceed if one was modified. Per-run access tokens, action inputs, fault text, and resubmitted-request ids prevent a hard-coded report from passing. No VMware endpoint is contacted.

api_contract.note: VCF Automation has no specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository. docs/contract.json was derived by reading the VCF Automation xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com and says so in its own source block; docs/official_sources.json records every page URL, the operation it documents and the date it was fetched.
